[2.5t²/2−4t]₂.₄⁴=v−0.
v=1.25(4²−2.4²)−4(4−2.4)=6.4m/s.

reviews.note: For a uniform solid sphere, the limiting coefficient is(2/7)tanθ, including equality. The printed strict condition is the intended threshold. A hollow or nonuniform sphere has a different inertia.
reviews.question: A sphere of massm rolls without slipping on a plane inclined atθ. Which condition should be satisfied for pure rolling?
reviews.explanation:
The required friction ratio isf/N=tanθ/[1+R²/k²],wherek is radius of gyration andI=mk².
For a uniform solid sphere,I=(2/5)mR²=mk², hencek²=(2/5)R².
f/N=tanθ/[1+R²/((2/5)R²)]=(2/7)tanθ.
Pure rolling requiresμs≥(2/7)tanθ. Option(b) gives the intended threshold using a strict inequality; equality is the limiting case. Other sphere mass distributions need their own moment of inertia.

reviews.note: For a steady full cycle travelling4A against constant frictionμN,the energy loss is4μNA. The additional printed claim of periodic free motion needs qualification because amplitudes decrease.
reviews.question: The energy dissipated during a full cycle by dry-friction damping,in terms of maximum amplitudeA and friction forceμN,is
reviews.explanation:
Dry-friction or Coulomb damping occurs at a sliding contact. Friction opposes relative velocity and depends on the normal force.
The source lists:nonlinear equation of motion;unchanged ideal sliding-segment frequency;oscillatory motion;eventual rest in free vibration;and linearly decreasing successive peak amplitudes. A decreasing-amplitude free response is not strictly periodic,though the ideal sliding half-cycles have equal durations.
For a full cycle travelling4A:
ΔW=μN×4A=4μNA.
The source also gives the harmonic-balance approximation for forced steady sliding:
A=(F₀/K)√{[1−(4μN/(πF₀))²]/[1−(ω/ωn)²]²}.
This is conditional on its sliding/forcing assumptions;it is not a general free-response amplitude formula.

reviews.sourceExplanation:
Dry Friction Damping(or)Coulomb Damping:Dry friction damping occurs at the interface between two bodies in relative motion with contact. As shown,the friction force opposes relative velocity and depends on normal force.
Characteristics:
• The equation of motion is nonlinear with Coulomb damping.
• Natural frequency is unchanged by Coulomb damping.
• Motion is periodic with Coulomb damping.
• The system comes to rest after some time with Coulomb damping.
• Amplitude reduces linearly with Coulomb damping.
Energy dissipated in a full cycle:ΔW=4μNA.
WhereA=(F₀/K){[1−(4μN/(πF₀))²]/[1−(ω/ωn)²]²}¹ᐟ².
